trials.notes: Correctly chose WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() and checked null. All API methods used are documented: next_token(), get_token_name(), get_token_type(), get_current_depth(), get_modifiable_text(), and is_tag_closer(). Strong #text-only collection with decoded text. Minor idiom issue: heading detection mostly relies on get_token_name() rather than first requiring #tag, but no runtime misuse or _doing_it_wrong records.

Correct processor choice and only documented API calls. It uses one token walk, #tag filtering for heading openers, #text-only text collection, and get_modifiable_text() for decoded content. Slightly less idiomatic because it stores heading depth but never uses it, relying entirely on matching closer tokens; this is valid with WP_HTML_Processor because next_token() documents virtual closers, but it is a narrower pattern than the depth-bounded subtree recipe.

Best alignment with the rendered docs: WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), single next_token() pass, explicit #tag and #text checks, decoded get_modifiable_text(), current-depth tracking, closer handling, and final flush. No hallucinated methods and no _doing_it_wrong records. Bookmarks, serialization, and get_updated_html() were not needed for this read-only extraction task.

failure_analysis: No hidden/frozen case failed in any trial: all three passed 7/7, with no _doing_it_wrong records. The docs did well at steering subjects to WP_HTML_Processor rather than WP_HTML_Tag_Processor for structure-aware text extraction. The decisive passages were the Tag Processor 'Which processor should I use?' section, the HTML Processor create_fragment() docs for BODY fragments, the 'collect DOM-style text from a subtree' recipe, get_modifiable_text()'s decoded-text contract, and next_token()/get_current_depth() guidance about virtual closers and depth-bounded walks. The implied-heading-close case was handled because next_token() documents that HTML Processor visits closers for implicitly closed and unclosed elements; a probe showed <h2>One<h3>Two produces an H2 closer before H3. Near-misses: trial-2's explanation frames the algorithm around matching source-like closers and leaves its depth variable unused, which would have been fragile if the docs had not explicitly promised virtual closers. Trial-1 uses get_token_name() as a tag-name detector without an explicit #tag guard; frozen cases are fine, but recipes would be clearer if they consistently paired tag-name checks with get_token_type() === '#tag' where non-tag tokens must be excluded. None of the candidates checked get_last_error() or paused_at_incomplete_token(); for this read-only task the docs allow caller-defined partial-result policy, but stricter extraction APIs would need a clearer pattern.

doc_gaps.problem: The virtual-closer behavior is documented, but the practical state-machine consequence is spread across next_token(), is_tag_closer(), and get_current_depth(). Subjects passed, but one relied on matching closers without using depth, which is easy to misunderstand.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact token trace for malformed or omitted-end-tag input showing opener, text, virtual closer, tag name, is_tag_closer(), and depth. State explicitly when closer-driven state machines are valid and when depth-bounded subtree scans are preferable.

doc_gaps.location: html-processor.md: repeated-region warning vs subtree text recipe
doc_gaps.problem: The docs warn against nested next_token() loops for repeated regions, while the subtree recipe shows a bounded inner walk. The distinction is subtle: a single bounded subtree scan is fine, but repeated sibling extraction should usually be one stateful pass.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short decision note distinguishing 'one bounded scan of a matched subtree' from 'extract many sibling regions'. Explain cursor position after the bounded loop exits and how to avoid skipping a boundary token.

doc_gaps.problem: Recipes vary between checking get_token_name() directly and guarding with get_token_type() === '#tag'. That leaves room for models to treat nodeName as a universal tag predicate.
doc_gaps.suggestion: In tag-matching examples, consistently show the #tag guard when the code must only match element tokens. Clarify the dynamic-name cases and align the text mentioning processing-instruction-style names with the listed token types.

doc_gaps.location: html-processor.md: subtree text extraction completion policy
doc_gaps.problem: The docs correctly say read-only extraction may choose how to handle paused or aborted scans, but they do not show a concise strict-vs-best-effort pattern. All candidates omitted get_last_error() and paused_at_incomplete_token(), which was acceptable here but could be wrong for stricter callers.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add two small generic snippets after the subtree text recipe: one returning accumulated best-effort text, and one rejecting or returning a sentinel when paused_at_incomplete_token() or get_last_error() indicates an incomplete scan.
